note: The raw PoC bytes are loaded as a text Lua chunk and then executed by the harness.
A return expression whose only value is a function call is recognized as a tail call.
The parser emits OP_TAILCALL for the PoC's return-call expression.
The VM executes the generated OP_TAILCALL instruction.

code: int b = GETARG_B(i);  /* number of arguments + 1 (function) */
note: The encoded argument count is read from the tail-call instruction.

code: luaD_pretailcall(L, ci, ra, b);  /* prepare call frame */
note: The Lua closure at register ra is passed to the tail-call frame preparation routine.
The callee prototype is selected from the closure being tail-called.

code: for (i = 0; i < narg1; i++)  /* move down function and arguments */
note: The callee closure and arguments are copied over the current CallInfo function slot before the CallInfo savedpc is updated to the callee's code.
This makes ci_func(ci)->p refer to the callee prototype while ci->u.l.savedpc still refers to the caller's instruction stream.
Stack growth is checked in the inconsistent-frame window created by the prior copy.
The macro routes the frame-size stack check into luaD_checkstackaux.
When the requested frame cannot fit, the stack growth path raises a Lua runtime error while the CallInfo still mixes callee closure with caller savedpc.
Error reporting asks for source-line information through the inconsistent CallInfo.
The callee prototype from ci_func(ci) is combined with the caller-relative currentpc, so debug-line lookup can index beyond the callee lineinfo array.
The mismatched pc indexes f->lineinfo past the callee prototype's valid debug-line entries, producing the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow read.
